rows.title: TRUNK-6795: Populate obs reference ranges in a save handler so they survive validation.disable
rows.excerpt:
ntouched observation and replace it with a revision differing only in the overwritten interpretation. An observation the caller has genuinely edited is already dirty by the time the handler sees it, so it is still re-interpreted.

The interpretation is therefore deliberately asymmetric, and this is documented on `ObsSaveHandler`: on a **new** observation an interpretation supplied by the caller is kept, so a client that computes its own interpretations wins; on an **amendment** it is overwritten, because a persisted observation offers no way to tell an interpretation the caller has just set from one derived on an earlier save, and re-interpreting an edited value is the more useful default. A client that maintains its own interpretations — a laboratory amending a result, say — has to set the interpretation again after every amendment.

Resolving a range is read-only, but it runs queries: the concept's ranges, and then whatever each range's criteria asks for (`$fn.getLatestObs` resolves a concept reference and searches observations). Because the handler now resolves a range while an edited `Obs` is still dirty in the Hibernate session, any of those queries would auto-flush that observation past `ImmutableEntityInterceptor`. `ConceptServiceImpl.getConceptReferenceRange` therefore holds the session in `FlushMode.MANUAL` for the whole resolution and restores the previous mode in a `finally`, the way `HibernateAdministrationDAO.validate` already did for the validator run that used to derive the range.

**Behaviour change for a concept with no bounds configured.** `ObsValidator` used to fall back to the `ConceptNumeric`'s own range fields when no `ConceptReferenceRange` matched, so a numeric observation whose concept has no bounds configured at all was saved with an all-null `obs_reference_range` row and an interpretation of `NORMAL`. Deriving the range through `ConceptService.getConceptReferenceRange` drops that fallback: its default range is null when every bound is null, so such an observation now gets neither a reference range nor an interpretation, since `NORMAL` derived from no bounds is not information. This will be most observations in an implementation that has not configured ranges. `handle_shouldSetNeitherReferenceRangeNorInterpretationForAConceptWithNoBoundsConfigured` pins it.
